deliverables: Ongoing maintenance including bug fixes, dependency upkeep, security patches, and releases
Dijkstra developer preview with initial Plutus V4 support in the compiler and standard library
Improved interfaces and documentation for JS/TS components embedded in MeshJS, Evolution SDK, and Lucid Evolution
Java/Kotlin integration examples for Spring Boot and Ktor and cleaner integration paths with Cardano Client Lib and Yaci
Dijkstra ledger rules and transaction-builder updates including new builtins, cost models, nested transactions, accounts, and guard scripts with conformance testing
Foundational runtime components, reactive workers, chain follower, and task scheduler
request.what: Fund a 9-month continuation of Scalus covering maintenance, Dijkstra hard-fork readiness, interoperability across JVM and JS/TS ecosystems, and a scoped application runtime.

claims.claim: Scalus is an established open-source Cardano development platform built by Lantr Engineering over three years of continuous delivery.
The proposal requests ₳2,464,844 for 9 months at a $0.16/ADA reference rate with no contingency.

The proposal is a reduced resubmission from a prior ₳8.503M 12-month proposal, reducing budget by 71%, FTE from 8.25 to 2.25, and removing the standalone L1 node, full L2 integration, broad formal verification, and advanced devnet expansion from scope.
Scalus components are reused in Cardano Client Lib, YaciDevKit, MeshJS SDK, Evolution SDK, and Lucid Evolution.
Protocols and applications listed as built on Scalus include Gummiworm L2, Bifrost, SugarRush, Vela, and DID/DIDComm.
The document states Scalus has 4,642 commits across 32 releases, 12 contributors, and more than 20,000 monthly Scalus.js downloads.

The funded work is planned as three quarterly milestones from July 2026 through March 2027, with maintenance running continuously and Dijkstra readiness, interoperability, and runtime work phased across the milestones.
Delivery is described as milestone-based and administered through audited SundaeSwap treasury contracts with an independent oversight board and third-party assurance.
Lantr Engineering says every prior milestone was delivered on time and commits to public reporting, open community sessions, and on-time milestone delivery for treasury-funded work.

The proposal argues Scalus aligns with Cardano 2030 by enabling developer infrastructure, open-source reuse, education, interoperability, and ecosystem growth rather than directly producing TVL, transactions, or active users itself.

summary: The document requests ₳2,464,844 for Lantr Engineering to continue Scalus for 9 months, focused on maintaining existing infrastructure, preparing for Dijkstra, improving interoperability, and delivering a scoped application runtime, with several adoption and governance claims mostly asserted by the proposer and some externally checkable metrics.
